text:
Truth, you ask? A slippery eel, that's what truth is! Always wriggling away, changing shape, hiding in plain sight. Like a particularly pungent cheese, it stinks to high heaven, but everyone insists on sniffing it anyway.

Some say truth is absolute, a shining beacon in the darkness. Ha! More like a flickering candle in a hurricane, blown this way and that, leaving only ashes and confusion in its wake.

Others claim truth is relative, a chameleon changing colors to suit its surroundings. A clever beast, that is, always adapting, always blending in. But if truth is so adaptable, can we ever truly know it? Or are we just chasing shadows on the wall?

Perhaps truth is a jest, a cosmic prank played on us by a mischievous god. We search for it, we grasp for it, we think we've found it, only to realize it was a figment of our imagination all along.

But hey, who am I to say? I'm just a jester, juggling absurdity and poking fun at the world. Maybe truth is just a word, a meaningless label we slap on things we don't understand.

Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a banana peel
